post.originalText:
I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to generate a animated preview of our book- Winning With AI.
The output is an included here with this post, which turned out to be way better than i thought it would produce. What do you think?

I dug a bit deeper into what's happening behind the scenes.
Claude Opus 5.5 produces them differently from models that come with a native video model.

A native video model like Google's Veo generates the pixels of the video directly from your prompt, whereas Opus 5.5 only takes text and images in and gives text out, so it writes the animation as code, usually one HTML file with SVG shapes and a timing library like GSAP, then looks at snapshots of its own frames, fixes what looks wrong, and renders the result out as a GIF or MP4. It never draws a pixel itself.

Because the output is code, text, charts and logos stay sharp and any change is a small edit rather than a fresh generation (note to self: this is why people can keep refining the same animation for 10 or 20 rounds). 

It is worth noting that most Opus 5.5 videos people share are motion graphics and app-style animations, and very few are realistic footage, which is still where dedicated video models do better.
